failures.triage_note: REGRESSION, confirmed live this run. Social\ActivityService::on_upload() (line ~198) contains `if ( in_array( $privacy, array( 'private', 'dm' ), true ) ) { return; }` -- this explicitly SKIPS creating an mvs_activity row for private uploads. This is the exact opposite of the D-row's documented contract, which states the 1.7.0 fix (fc31bf0) made private uploads WRITE a row (only the BP sitewide mirror stays privacy-gated). Reproduced live: uploaded 'Smoke Upload Private' (media_id=135, privacy=private) via the real /my-media/ dashboard as owner -- zero rows in mvs_activity for media_id=135, confirmed by direct query immediately after upload (last activity id stayed at 72, no id=73 was ever created). By contrast, uploading the same file at privacy=public and privacy=members in the same session both correctly wrote activity rows (ids 71, 72). A pre-existing seed row (media_id=124, private, activity id=66) does have a row, but that was seeded by an older process before this regression -- it is not evidence the current code path works; the current code path was directly exercised via the real dashboard UI and failed.
failures.expected: Uploading a media item with privacy=private writes exactly one row to mvs_activity for it (SELECT * FROM mvs_activity WHERE media_id = $ID returns 1 row), per the documented 1.7.0 fix and the D-row contract. Only the BP sitewide activity mirror should stay privacy-gated, not the native mvs_activity table.
failures.actual: Uploading privacy=private via /my-media/ writes ZERO rows to mvs_activity. ActivityService::on_upload() bare-returns for privacy in ('private','dm') before ever calling record(). Public and members uploads in the same session correctly wrote activity rows.
failures.screenshot: n/a - server-side/DB-verified defect, no visual signature

failures.triage_note:
Coding Rule 11 violation ('No silent render fallthrough... every return; inside a render path must be paired with a visible empty state'). render_album() in Shortcodes.php delegates entirely to render_block_template('album-viewer', ...) -> build/blocks/album-viewer/render.php, which does a bare `if ( ! $album_id ) { return; }` with zero output. Contrast with the sibling [mvs_collection] shortcode, which handles its own no-id case directly in Shortcodes.php and returns a friendly '

Please provide a collection ID: [mvs_collection id="123"]

' message. [mvs_album] with a VALID id (tested id=17, 'Mountain Escapes') renders correctly (title, description, grid) -- only the missing/invalid-id empty-state branch is broken. Same underlying render.php is shared by the mvs/album-viewer block, so the block has the identical empty-state gap.
failures.expected: [mvs_album] (and the mvs/album-viewer block) with no id or an invalid id produces a visible empty-state message, matching the pattern used by the sibling [mvs_collection] shortcode.
failures.actual: [mvs_album] and [mvs_album id="999999"] (nonexistent) render nothing at all -- zero output, no message, no visible empty state. Verified via a temporary WP-CLI-seeded test page (torn down after the check).
failures.screenshot: n/a - defect is the absence of any rendered output

failures.triage_note: Coding Rule 11 violation. build/blocks/media-player/render.php gates `if ( ! $is_video && ! $is_audio ) { return; }` with zero output for image-type media -- no 'unsupported media type' message, no fallback image display. Verified against media_id=61 (real, existing, public image, title 'tiny'): [mvs_player id="61"] renders nothing. Historical findings-history F10 (2026-04-23) described this as a shortcode-vs-block DIVERGENCE where the shortcode rendered the image fine and only the block failed; that is no longer true -- both paths now share render_block_template() -> the same render.php, so the shortcode has regressed to the same silent-empty behavior as the block. Same render.php backs the mvs/media-player block, so the block has the identical gap.
failures.expected: [mvs_player id="<image media>"] (and the mvs/media-player block) either renders the image as a fallback, or shows a visible 'this media type is not playable here' message -- never a bare empty output, per Coding Rule 11 and the render-state-rules standing contract.
failures.actual: [mvs_player id="61"] against a real, existing, public IMAGE media item renders zero output -- no image, no message, no visible empty state.
failures.screenshot: n/a - defect is the absence of any rendered output

The STANDALONE single-media page (/media/<slug>/) has its OWN, separate reaction-bar markup that does not carry the same a11y wiring: aria-label values are bare lowercase words ('like','love',...) with no aria-pressed attribute at all, and the wrapping [role="group"] has no aria-label. Included for rigor since this page is a real, frequently-shared customer surface, distinct from the tested-and-passing lightbox.

failures.triage_note: Low severity, no customer-facing impact -- the real, displayed comment count comes from mvs_media_stats.comments, which DOES update correctly and is what MediaController's REST response and the grid UI actually read. mvs_media_index.comment_count is a SEPARATE denormalized column, defined in the schema (Migrator) and listed in MediaRepository's field allowlist, but no writer anywhere in includes/ ever updates it after its default 0 -- confirmed via full-codebase grep. Contrast with the sibling reaction_count column, which ReactionService explicitly keeps in sync with an inline comment documenting the intent ('Keep the denormalized reaction_count in mvs_media_index in sync'). CommentService has no equivalent line. Flagging per the plugin's own coding rule ('any store written but never read, or defined but never written, is dead weight') -- worth a one-line fix or removing the column, not a release blocker.
failures.expected: mvs_media_index.comment_count either stays in sync with real comment activity (matching the reaction_count pattern) or is removed if genuinely unused.
failures.actual: Posted a real comment on media_id=133 (fixture, deleted after verification) via the lightbox composer -- mvs_media_stats.comments correctly went 0 to 1, but mvs_media_index.comment_count stayed at 0.

R3 / D.search-empty-state: /explore-media/?s=zzznoresults999 still hard-404s. Confirmed origin='for' this run by reproducing the identical 404 on /sample-page/?s=test (a stock WordPress page with zero plugin markup), while the WordPress-native /?s=test search on the homepage works fine. This isolates the fault to this site's permalink/rewrite routing for '<page>/?s=' combinations specifically, not to wpmediaverse's own explore.php template (whose search-empty-state code is present and correct, just never reached). Needs a server/hosting-side look at rewrite rules, not a plugin code change.
F.rtl (Arabic/RTL rendering of Explore/single-media/profile/dashboard/lightbox) not exercised this run.

Frontend dark mode: emulateMedia(colorScheme:'dark') produced no visual change (--mvs-bg stayed #ffffff in both light and dark emulation). Verified via source that this is INTENTIONAL, not a bug -- assets/css/frontend.css line ~141 documents 'Dark mode: theme-controlled only (no prefers-color-scheme)', gated behind theme-supplied variables (--reign-site-body-bg-color etc.). The active theme on this site (Twenty Twenty-Five) has no dark-mode class/attribute hook, so no dark styling applies -- expected on this theme, would need a Reign-theme (or equivalent dark-mode-aware theme) site to actually exercise the plugin's dark-mode CSS branch.

Media 64 (BunnyCDN) frontend serving: the single-media page and REST thumbnail_url/file_url for media_id=64 route through the LOCAL /wp-json/mvs/v1/serve proxy rather than a direct mediaverse1.b-cdn.net link, even though R2 (Admin Details page links) is now fixed and correctly shows direct CDN hrefs. The image itself loads correctly (200, real bytes, naturalWidth=800) so there is no visible defect, but this differs from the 1.4.0 'location-based media display' direct-CDN-for-public-cloud-media design. Plausible explanation: the direct-CDN bypass requires a cloud StorageDriver class to resolve eligibility, and those classes ship in Pro (deactivated for this free-mode run) -- needs confirmation against a combo-mode run before treating as a gap.
